q: How must pipe laid in the ground be supported?
o: On a firm bed for its whole length, or on a concrete cradle
On wooden blocks at each joint
On loose rocks from the excavation
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Gaps under the pipe let it sag, crack and collect solids.

q: What is done to burred pipe and tube ends?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Burrs narrow the bore and catch solids.

q: How is horizontal plastic pipe 51 mm and larger supported?
o: With stiff metal or wood backing along its length
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Plastic tube 38 mm and smaller needs continuous backing because it sags.

q: Which piping connections are prohibited?
o: Those that retard or obstruct the flow of air, water or sewage
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Anything that narrows the path causes blockages or trap siphonage.

q: How large must a sleeve driven through the ground for a pipe be?
o: At least one pipe size larger than the pipe
The same size as the pipe
One size smaller than the pipe
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: The pipe must slide through the sleeve without damage.

q: How are valves, pipes and fittings installed?
o: In the correct relation to the direction of flow
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Check valves, wyes and cleanouts only work one way.

q: Which of these protects pipe from corrosion?
o: Leaving the pipe bare in wet soil
Inside lining, outside coating, good bedding and a top shield
Laying it against a concrete footing
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Protection depends on the pipe and the soil.

q: After a repair, what is done with openings left in drainage or vent piping?
o: They are left open for air
They are permanently capped or plugged
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Open holes leak sewer gas.

q: How is the space between a pipe and its sleeve through a wall sealed?
o: With a sealant such as bituminous material
With cement mortar packed hard around the pipe
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: The seal keeps water and pests out while letting the pipe move.

q: What does IPS mean?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Plumbing abbreviations: IPS iron pipe size, PE polyethylene, PB polybutylene, B&S bell and spigot.

q: How close to a footing may a trench deeper than the footing run?
o: Outside a 45° line drawn down from the bottom edge of the footing
Anywhere, if the soil is dry
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Digging inside the 45° zone removes soil that supports the footing.

q: What does PE mean in pipe materials?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Plumbing abbreviations: IPS iron pipe size, PE polyethylene, PB polybutylene, B&S bell and spigot.

q: Where may waste water NOT be disposed of?
o: At any place not approved for it
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Waste water dumped on the ground or into a canal is a health hazard.

q: What does B&S mean for cast iron pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Plumbing abbreviations: IPS iron pipe size, PE polyethylene, PB polybutylene, B&S bell and spigot.

q: What minimum slope may a horizontal drain 102 mm and larger have where 2% is impractical?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Smaller drains must stay at 2%.

q: What is oakum?
o: Hemp treated with oil or tar, used to pack joints
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Oakum is packed into cast iron hubs before molten lead is poured.

q: Which bend makes a 45° change of direction?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Drainage bends: 1/16 bend = 22.5°, 1/8 bend = 45°, 1/6 bend = 60°.

q: What is a pipeline welder?
o: A welder who specializes in welding pipe
A plumber who only threads pipe
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Welded steel pipe for water and fire lines needs welders certified for pipe work.

q: What must be true of every plumbing fixture?
o: It drains to the storm drain
It is properly connected to the drainage system
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Every fixture must discharge to an approved drain.

q: How often is horizontal threaded pipe 25 mm and larger supported?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Support spacing for horizontal pipe: threaded pipe 25 mm and up every 3.6 m; copper 51 mm and up every 3.0 m; cast iron soil pipe at every joint, within 1.5 m of it; lead pipe along its whole length.

q: What must be done with industrial waste?
o: Treat it, and never discharge it untreated to the ground or waterways
Discharge it straight to a canal
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Industrial waste can poison water and soil.

q: How is horizontal lead pipe supported?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Support spacing for horizontal pipe: threaded pipe 25 mm and up every 3.6 m; copper 51 mm and up every 3.0 m; cast iron soil pipe at every joint, within 1.5 m of it; lead pipe along its whole length.

q: What does the code require of workmanship?
o: Accepted engineering practice, with no defects hidden
Defects may be hidden if the work passes the test
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Cracks and holes must be fixed, not concealed.

q: How is horizontal plastic tube 38 mm and smaller supported?
o: With stiff metal or wood backing along its length
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Small plastic tube sags between hangers, so it rests on continuous backing.

q: May a vent pipe be used as a soil or waste pipe?
o: No, and a drain may not be used as a vent either
Yes, if it is cast iron
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Each system must do its own job.

q: What clear height must a piping tunnel have above the pipe?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: A worker must be able to reach the pipe.

q: What must gate and check valves have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Valves wear out and must be reachable.

q: How is a trench backfilled over pipe?
o: By dumping all soil at once
With rocks placed directly on the pipe
In layers, with special care in the zone 0.30 m above the pipe
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Heavy stones dropped on the pipe crack it.

q: What must each building have for its drainage?
o: Its own connection to an approved public or private sewer
A shared connection through a neighbour's lot
A connection to the storm drain
No connection, if it has a septic tank shared by the block
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Plumbing may not cross onto another lot.

q: How is pipe protected where it passes through concrete or masonry?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Building movement would crack a pipe cast solid in concrete.

q: How is pipe length measured?
o: From end to end of the fittings only
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Centerline length is the developed length used in sizing.

q: What does the code say about plumbing and the structure?
o: Beams may be cut to fit pipes
Columns may be drilled at will
Footings may be undermined if backfilled
No structural member may be weakened by plumbing work
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Holes in beams and columns need the structural engineer's approval.

q: What does PB mean in pipe materials?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Plumbing abbreviations: IPS iron pipe size, PE polyethylene, PB polybutylene, B&S bell and spigot.

q: How deep is a building sewer laid below finished ground?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: It is at least 0.30 m deep, and 0.60 m from the building wall.

q: Why does PVC pipe come in different colors?
o: To tell pressure water pipe from drainage pipe
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Makers often use blue or white for pressure water pipe and gray or orange for drainage, but always check the printed markings.

q: What is the standard slope of horizontal drains smaller than 102 mm?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Small drains need the full 2% to carry solids.

q: What parts make up a slip joint?
o: A compression nut, compression washer and friction ring
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Slip joints are used on trap and tailpiece connections.

q: Which bend makes a 22.5° change of direction?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Drainage bends: 1/16 bend = 22.5°, 1/8 bend = 45°, 1/6 bend = 60°.

q: What is a welded (seam) joint?
o: A joint sealed with oakum and lead
A joint sealed with a rubber ring
A joint where metal parts are joined in a molten state
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Welding melts the metals together.

q: Which bend makes a 60° change of direction?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Drainage bends: 1/16 bend = 22.5°, 1/8 bend = 45°, 1/6 bend = 60°.

q: Where is horizontal cast iron soil pipe supported?
o: At each joint, within 1.5 m of it
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Support spacing for horizontal pipe: threaded pipe 25 mm and up every 3.6 m; copper 51 mm and up every 3.0 m; cast iron soil pipe at every joint, within 1.5 m of it; lead pipe along its whole length.

q: Where there is no public sewer, where does sewage go?
o: To an approved private system such as a septic tank
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Where a public sewer is available, connection is required.

q: How often is horizontal copper tubing 51 mm and larger supported?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Support spacing for horizontal pipe: threaded pipe 25 mm and up every 3.6 m; copper 51 mm and up every 3.0 m; cast iron soil pipe at every joint, within 1.5 m of it; lead pipe along its whole length.

q: Where may plumbing NOT be placed?
o: Where it interferes with the normal use of the building
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Ch. 2 and Ch. 3
n: Pipes must not block doors, windows or other building functions.
